questions.q: Why do these items have no icon?
lines: Before this round, an item wore an icon only when the Gabe Universe draws a node of its kind. It draws functions, tables, schemas, hooks and middleware. It draws no rate limit, check, fork or catch, so those were bare words.

Now each gate names the function or the middleware it runs in, with that element's icon and role. The gate itself wears an icon of this page's own, one per kind; which icons is one of your calls (gate icons).
A function always wears the function icon now, even when no role is known for it.
Items without an icon in BY MOMENT on {ep}: {bareBefore} before this round, {bareNow} after round 1b. In the Gates row: {gateBefore}, then {gateNow}. In Functions: {fnBefore}, then {fnNow}.
What the measure still finds without one: {bareNowRows}.
questions.subject: page

questions.about: sensitive and global, at the edge
questions.verdict: Q: what is this — a function?
lines: No. They are {nLim} counters, the {sName} counter and the {gName} counter: objects of the class {limClass} (in the code: {sCode} and {gCode}). The server builds them once, when it starts ({mwFile}: line {initS} for the {sName} counter, line {initG} for the {gName} counter).
They belong to {mwName}, a middleware: code every request passes through before any endpoint runs. Its method {mwMethod} asks each counter if this client's IP is over its limit.
The {sName} counter: the {sPrefixN} path prefixes on its sensitive list, this one among them ({sEndpoints} endpoints). At most {sLimit} requests in {sWindow} seconds. Checked at line {sLine}, first.
The {gName} counter: every path but {gExempt} ({gEndpoints} endpoints). At most {gLimit} requests in {gWindow} seconds. Checked at line {gLine}, after the {sName} counter.
Over a limit, the answer is {limStatus} “{limDetail}” and the endpoint never runs. Both counters run only when rate limiting is switched on, or in production ({limSwitch}).

questions.verdict: Q: what is fetching and from where?
lines: The hook that sends this request is {sender}, a {senderKind}. It sends {sendMethod} {sendPath}.
When the answer is a success ({invWhen}), it refreshes the saved answers under the key {invKey} ({invAt}). A refresh throws those answers away, so a screen that shows them fetches them again.
{nRefetch} hooks keep a saved answer under that key, so this is what is fetched: {refetchList}.
This request writes {writes}. {readsList}

@statuses

questions.q: What are we representing in standard or specialist?
questions.verdict: Q: what are we representing in standard or specialist?
lines: The row answers one question: is this endpoint built like the others, and what is unusual about it?

An endpoint is made of pieces: its method, each status it can answer, reading a body, its login, its rate limit, its catches, its switches, a repeat key. Each piece is counted across the app's {nEp} endpoints. The rule: {pieceRule}.
{ep} has {nPieces} pieces: {nNorm} the norm, {nCommon} common, {nRare} rare, {nOnly} only here. It lacks {nLacks} of the norms.
Its rare pieces are what is unusual: {rareList}.

Its switches ({switchKinds}) are not unusual: {switchLine}. A switch is set by the server's settings and changes a way the request can go. So by my pick a switch stands in Gates and decisions beside what it switches, and a rare piece becomes a label on the item it names.

lines: An in-flight value is something the code keeps outside a local variable, so a later moment can use what an earlier moment put there. It is not a flag stored in the database.
This request carries {nInf}: {nReq} go with the answer, {nSrv} are kept by the server between requests.
@inflightReq
Kept by the server: {srvNames}. Of these, {srvDecNames} are read where the {srvDecStatus} endings are checked ({srvDecLines}).

questions.q: Why do these functions have no role?
questions.about: This answer is about the map, not the code, so it lives here and not on the page (D-017).
lines: A function's role comes from the Gabe Universe, and the Universe draws only what the code map reads. The code map reads {nScanned} folders of apps/api: {scannedList}.
@named
Folders the forms feed reaches that the code map does not read: {unreadDirs}.

Where no source knows a role, the page now uses the station's own rule on the feed: accessor when a function reads or writes a table in its own body, gate by the station's name rule. Otherwise a function wears its icon and its name, and its hover says what it does.
The fix is to widen what gustify's code map reads. That is a change in gustify, and it waits: work stays in the suite for now.
